caption: Figure 3 Hierarchical architecture of El Agente Q. Inter-agent communication is illustrated with black arrows, where solid arrows represent task delegation from higher-level agents, and dotted arrows indicate feedback and reporting from lower-level agents.The agents can be broadly categorized into three functional modules -the geometry module (coral), the quantum calculation module (blue), and the file I/O module (yellow). Each module can be thought of as a department in a complex organization with its own manager, employees, and tools (violet). For example, the geometry generation agent gets to decide if the system should be handled by the organometallic complexes agent or Perplexity AI search (78), and decide the charge and multiplicity of the system.

This expansion includes the incorporation of user-friendly interfaces-such as enabling users to draw and manipulate molecular structures directly, similar to the functionality provided by tools like JMol (90; 91), ChemDoodle (92), and ChemDraw (93)-thereby making the system more flexible and accessible to a broader range of academic and industrial researchers (Stage 2). Another key development in the initial stage of El Agente Q will be the expansion of its current toolkit to include spectroscopic property predictions, reaction mechanisms, photochemical processes, and high-level single-and multi-reference electronic structure methods as well as excited state methods, such as DLPNO-CCSD(T) (94), MC-PDFT (95), ADC(2) (96; 97) and NEVPT2 (98) (Stage 3).
Figure 4 El Agente Q Development Roadmap: Bridging Molecular Properties, Advanced Simulations, and Self-Driving Lab Integration. The milestones are not drawn to timescale.
